explanation: An ancient Phoenician city described as a major trading center and powerful maritime nation in Isaiah 23.
A metaphor for God's power and influence, used to describe how He punishes or rewards people and nations.
In this context, it refers to God's judgment on Tyre, where He will destroy the city and its wealth because of their pride and sin.
The period mentioned in Isaiah 23 during which Tyre must suffer under destruction before it can rise again as a trading city.
A symbol of forgetfulness and loss of culture and identity resulting from the destruction of Tyre.
The wealth and resources gathered from trade and shipping, which after Tyre's restoration will be dedicated to the Lord.
Another name for God, the Almighty Creator who, according to the Bible, rules over the universe and all its creatures.
